_about: Samples and discoveries (core-loop step 5, docs/samples-lab-journal.md). A discovery matches samples by kind, rock, unit and in_cave, or by any entry in match. need: matching samples from different spots to confirm (common 3, uncommon 2, rare 1); field: logged straight from chapter one. bonus: multipliers the sim reads through MHSamples.bonus().

unit_rocks._about: Rock types by the geology unit a rock sits on (region.json geology, MHSiteTerrain.geology_unit), or by the cave it's in (lava_tube, cave, ice_cave). A sample within find_reach of a cave's find spot is that find's rock instead.

unit_regolith._about: What a regolith sample can show beyond the usual, by unit: bound water in clays, sulfates and icy ground.

site_rocks._about: The old single-site maps (legacy in data/sites.json), by site id.

discoveries.label: Water ice in the ground
discoveries.text: A core found clean ice under the dust. Water for drinking, for oxygen, for growing food.
discoveries.reply: The Geology team is delighted: ground ice, confirmed by hand. The extractor plan is yours.

discoveries.label: Water from Mars ice
discoveries.text: The extractor and the reclaimer keep the crew in water without Earth's stores.
discoveries.reply: First water made on Mars for a crew. Well done.

discoveries.label: Oxygen from Mars water
discoveries.text: Splitting the extracted water keeps the crew breathing.
discoveries.reply: Oxygen self-sufficient. The Humans team has framed the readout.

discoveries.label: Washed soil grows plants
discoveries.text: Rinsed of its perchlorate, Mars regolith grew a seedling.
discoveries.reply: A seedling in Mars soil. The Life team asks for photos. Lots of photos.

discoveries.label: Perchlorate in the soil
discoveries.lead: Possible perchlorate in the soil
discoveries.text: The soil holds perchlorate salts: toxic to people, but they wash out, and they can even be a source of oxygen.
discoveries.reply: Confirmed across the site. The Life team has tuned the washing: growing beds do better.

discoveries.label: Iron-oxide dust
discoveries.lead: The dust may be mostly iron oxide
discoveries.text: The fine dust is mostly iron oxide, finer than flour, and it clings with static.
discoveries.reply: Knowing the dust helps. Mission Control has a better cleaning angle for the arrays.

discoveries.label: Water bound in the soil
discoveries.lead: The soil may hold bound water
discoveries.text: Minerals in this soil hold water in their crystals. Heated, it comes out.
discoveries.reply: Bound water: a second source. The intake team is very interested.

discoveries.label: Dust layers in the ice
discoveries.lead: The ice may record past dust storms
discoveries.text: Thin dark bands in the ice: dust from storms, laid down year by year.
discoveries.reply: A storm record. The Climate team can now see storms coming sooner.

discoveries.label: Ice from an older climate
discoveries.text: Deep ice, laid down when Mars tilted differently and the climate was another.
discoveries.reply: Old ice. The Climate team is going through it layer by layer.

discoveries.label: Basalt bedrock
discoveries.lead: The bedrock looks volcanic
discoveries.text: Dark volcanic rock. Most of the surface of Mars is made of it.
discoveries.reply: Knowing the basalt, the printer team has tuned the mix: shielding prints faster.

discoveries.label: Vesicular basalt
discoveries.lead: Some rocks are full of holes
discoveries.text: Full of holes left by gas bubbles as the lava cooled.
discoveries.reply: Lava flows, then. The Geology team wonders where they came from.

discoveries.label: Dust-coated rock
discoveries.lead: The rocks wear a coat of dust
discoveries.text: Mars dust coats everything orange. Under it, the rock is grey.
discoveries.reply: Noted. The rust is only skin deep.

discoveries.label: Olivine
discoveries.lead: Green crystals in the basalt
discoveries.text: Olivine breaks down quickly in water, so this ground has been dry for a very long time.
discoveries.reply: Olivine: a dry place, for a long time. A clue for where not to look for water.

discoveries.label: Salt crust
discoveries.lead: A pale crust of salts
discoveries.text: Salts left behind as water evaporated: harmful to people, which is why suits get cleaned.
discoveries.reply: Salt where water dried. Keep the suits clean.

discoveries.label: Hematite concretions
discoveries.lead: Little iron-rich balls in the rock
discoveries.text: Small iron-rich balls that formed in water. Opportunity found thousands of them.
discoveries.reply: Blueberries! Water stood here once. The Geology team wants to know where it went.

discoveries.label: Gypsum veins
discoveries.lead: White veins through the rock
discoveries.text: A white mineral left by water trickling through cracks in the rock.
discoveries.reply: Water moving underground, long ago. The Climate team is drawing timelines.

discoveries.label: River conglomerate
discoveries.lead: Rounded pebbles cemented together
discoveries.text: Smooth, rounded stones cemented together: an ancient riverbed, like the one Curiosity found.
discoveries.reply: A river ran here. A big one.

discoveries.label: Sandstone layers
discoveries.lead: Fine layered sand turned to stone
discoveries.text: Layers of wind- and water-laid sand, turned to stone over ages.
discoveries.reply: Layered sandstone: pages of climate history.

discoveries.label: Lakebed mudstone
discoveries.lead: Fine mud layers, maybe from a lake
discoveries.text: Fine layers of mud from an old lake: good places to look for signs of ancient life.
discoveries.reply: A lake, once. The Life team would like every layer you can reach.

discoveries.label: Impact breccia
discoveries.lead: Shattered rock, welded back together
discoveries.text: Rock smashed by an impact and welded back together by the heat.
discoveries.reply: Impact rock. The crater's story starts here.

discoveries.label: Clay-rich rock
discoveries.text: Clay forms in water that isn't too acidic or salty: water that life could have used.
discoveries.reply: Clay. The Life team is very quiet, which means very excited.

discoveries.label: Pure sulfur
discoveries.text: Bright yellow crystals. In 2024 Curiosity cracked a rock open and found pure sulfur inside.
discoveries.reply: Sulfur, pure. Nobody expected that, on Earth or here.

discoveries.label: Iron meteorite
discoveries.text: A lump of iron and nickel from space. Rovers have found several lying on Mars.
discoveries.reply: A visitor from the asteroid belt. Mission Control wants it kept safe.

discoveries.label: Ice in the caves
discoveries.lead: There may be ice that lasts underground
discoveries.text: Ice in the shade of a cave, where the sun never reaches it. It may have been there for a very long time.
discoveries.reply: Two caves, both with ice. The Climate team thinks caves may keep ice that the surface lost long ago.

discoveries.label: Mineral crust in the caves
discoveries.lead: A pale crust on the cave walls
discoveries.text: Sulfates and opal, laid down on the walls by water seeping through the rock. On Earth, crusts like these can hold traces of microbes.
discoveries.reply: The same crust in two caves. The Life team would like it handled very carefully: if anything ever lived here, this is where it might show.

discoveries.label: Unweathered basalt
discoveries.text: Basalt the dust and wind never reached: the lava as it cooled, sealed in the tube's walls.
discoveries.reply: Pristine basalt. The Geology team can date the flow from it.

discoveries.label: Layered sediments
discoveries.lead: The canyon walls may be a record in layers
discoveries.text: Layer on layer of sediment, laid down by water and wind and cut open by the canyon: thousands of years per layer.
discoveries.reply: The canyon is a book. The Climate team wants samples from as many layers as you can reach.

discoveries.label: A steady climate underground
discoveries.lead: The deep cave may stay at one temperature
discoveries.text: Deep in the lava tube the suit's readings barely change between day and night, and the rock overhead blocks most of the radiation.
discoveries.reply: Steady temperature, a metres-thick roof. The Humans team has started a file called 'A place to live'.

discoveries.label: The air outside
discoveries.lead: The thin air changes with the sun
discoveries.reading_text: The suit logged the air out here: pressure, temperature and what it's made of. Log it again at %s, away from the base, to compare.
discoveries.text: Away from the base the suit logged the air by day and by night: 95 % carbon dioxide at under 1 % of Earth's pressure, rising and falling with the temperature. Thin, but it's everywhere.
discoveries.reply: Good readings. MOXIE showed oxygen can be split from that air, so the Humans team has sent the plan for an atmosphere processor.
